hook_text: You walk past it every day. But could you map it so a stranger understands it in ten seconds?
clip_script: Geographers turn the world into symbols. A dot for a tap. A line for a road. A shaded patch for a soccer field. Blue for water, green for plants. Then the rule that catches everyone: if it is on the map, it must be in the key. Next, which way is north? Check your shadow at midday; it points south. Draw your compass rose. Now pace the street outside your school. Two hundred metres, drawn four centimetres long: one centimetre equals fifty metres. That is your scale. Finally, walk around and record what the land is used for: houses, shops, workshops, parks, the clinic, the food garden. Put it all together and your neighbourhood becomes a map anyone can read.
visual_style: A whiteboard street turning into symbols one by one: a dot tap, a line road, a green patch; a key box filling up; a compass rose spinning to north; a scale bar marked 0, 50, 100 m.
pacing: Brisk build, each element snapping into place.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and start your map project.
